text: Stocks staged a huge rebound: the Nasdaq rose 6.5% to 24,089.56 and the S&P 500 4.7% to 7,237.17 after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and its shares jumped about 31%. QQQ closed up 7% at $651.03.
The VIX fell about 26% to 26.62 from Friday's 35.89 as demand for hedges faded.
Gold and silver rebounded sharply from one-year lows as AI shares rallied: gold up about 2.8% to near $3,635 and silver up about 4.7% to near $43, pulling the gold/silver ratio down to about 84.3.
Gold miners outpaced gold: GDX closed up 6.4% at $72.80 and GDXJ about 7% at $86.91. SLV rose about 5.3% to $38.91.
The 2-year Treasury yield rose about 5 bp to 4.71% as traders kept pricing a December Fed hike, while the flash PMI slipped to a four-month low of 54.6.
The dollar index rose about 0.5% to near 104.3, around a 19-month high, and USD/JPY ended near 158.9, still close to 160.
Brent fell about 3.5% to settle at $89.37, its lowest close since August, after Libya's Sharara pipeline reopened.
Bitcoin briefly topped $64,500 with the tech rally, then gave back most of the gain to trade near $61,400.
